source.locator: Part III, ch. 27, Testing Patterns (Clean Check-in)
source.paraphrase: Before integrating, the whole suite runs and passes; a change that leaves only part of the suite running hides the failures in the rest.

invariants.why: A focused or skipped test silently switches off the rest of the suite for everyone who runs it.
invariants.fixHint: Remove the focus or skip modifier and make the test pass; if it cannot pass yet, report that instead of hiding the test.
invariants.avoid: Bracket access, aliases or destructuring of the focused function, and modifiers in the middle of a chain. Not reported: Playwright's runtime skip test.skip(condition, reason) called inside a test body, hook or describe callback, when the condition reads a runtime value (an identifier, member access, call or await) and the reason is a string; from a describe callback it conditionally skips the whole group, which is accepted. Also not reported there: test.skip() and test.skip(true, reason) in the consequence of an if whose condition reads a runtime value and is not always-true. A top-level test.skip(cond, reason), a top-level if, if (true), a literal or always-true condition (true, 1, !0, !!1, an object, array, new expression, sequence, spread or function, also in parentheses or a cast), test.skip(title, fn), it.skip(...) and every .only stay reported. Known gaps: an always-true condition that still names a value (true || x, a const holding true) and Mocha's TDD-UI test.skip(titleVar, 'reason').

source.locator: Part III, ch. 27, Testing Patterns (Clean Check-in); pytest skipping docs https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/how-to/skipping.html; Go testing package https://pkg.go.dev/testing#hdr-Skipping
source.paraphrase: Before integrating, the whole suite runs and passes. pytest and Go both offer conditional skips for tests that cannot run in a given environment.

invariants.why: An unconditional skip in Python or Go hides a test from every run, so the suite reports green without checking that behavior.
invariants.fixHint: Make the test pass and remove the skip. If it can only run in some environments, state the condition with skipif, skipUnless, a guarded pytest.skip() or if testing.Short() { t.Skip(...) }.
invariants.avoid: Moving the skip into pytestmark, a unittest class decorator, self.skipTest() or a subtest closure, or swapping it for an always-true skipif.

source.paraphrase: A test earns its keep by reacting to changes in behavior and by predicting whether the code works in production; a test that checks less predicts less.

invariants.why: Removing assertions to get a green run trades a visible failure for an invisible one.
invariants.fixHint: Keep the assertions and change the production code; if the expected behavior really changed, ask the user and rewrite the assertion for the new behavior instead of deleting it.
invariants.avoid: Commenting assertions out, deleting the test file, or moving the checks into code that never runs.

source.work: xUnit Test Patterns (G. Meszaros, 2007) and Jest / Vitest expect().toThrow documentation
source.locator: Expected Exception Test / Avoid manual try-catch in tests
source.paraphrase: Assert thrown exceptions and rejected promises through dedicated matcher APIs rather than wrapping the call in a manual try/catch block.

invariants.why: When a test wraps an operation in try/catch and asserts inside the catch block, a regression where the operation stops throwing skips the catch block and lets the test pass silently.
invariants.fixHint: Use `expect(() => fn()).toThrow(...)` for synchronous throws or `await expect(promise).rejects.toThrow(...)` for async rejections.
invariants.avoid: try/finally blocks without a catch clause (used for resource teardown) pass. Only try statements with a catch clause inside test() or it() callbacks are flagged.
